title: Parser text node data modification also needs to fire children changed steps
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#insert-a-character

> If there is a [Text](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text) node immediately before insertionLocation, then append data to that [Text](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text) node's [data](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-cd-data).

If implemented exactly as written, excluding the children change steps, this can cause failures. E.g. in [xhr/formdata/constructor-formelement.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/xhr/formdata/constructor-formelement.html) we have

```html
  <textarea name="submit-me-16">textarea value
with linebreaks set to LF</textarea>
```

If your parser pauses after `<textarea name="submit-me-16">textarea`, and then later appends the rest, but never runs the children changed steps, then the textarea's raw value stays as `textarea`, instead of expanding to `textarea value\nwith linebreaks set to LF`. ([This happens in a jsdom PR](https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom/actions/runs/30698868971/job/91366231746?pr=3296#step:6:10867).)

However, if you instead use [replace data](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-cd-replace), you fire MutationObservers, which mismatches browsers.

So the spec needs to either:

- Manually call the children changed steps during parsing; or
- Factor out most of replace data except for MutationObservers, and use that algorithm. (E.g., a _suppressObservers_ optional argument would do the trick.)

Note that in theory there is a difference between these two options: the latter adjusts live ranges, and the former does not. However in this specific case the live range adjustments are a no-op (because we're always just appending), so they're the same.
